messages:
maria: heads up, seeing a spike in client errors from model-pull workers in us-west-2, seems correlated with a NAT gateway metric jump.  logs attached below.

maria: ```
2026-03-18T10:12:03Z worker-42 curl: (7) Failed to connect to 10.0.0.5 port 443: Connection reset by peer
2026-03-18T10:12:03Z kernel: tcp 0 0 10.0.0.6:54321->34.56.78.90:443 FIN_WAIT2
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z proxy: dial tcp: cannot assign requested address
``` 

jon: ugh, classic ephemeral port exhaustion. What are natgw active connection counts and port usage distributions?

maria: NATGW active connections jumped from ~12k -> 62k and ephemeral ports in aws metrics look pegged around 65500 allocated for that ENI pool. conntrack on sidecarsshows alot of TIME_WAIT piling up.

alex: are these short-lived fetches? model pulls happen in parallel, we recently increased concurrency to 50 per pod.

maria: yep, model pulls + healthcheck fanout. each worker tries 20 parallel pulls during startup.  :grimacing:

kevin: quick mitigation: reduce client concurrency and enable connection reuse / keepalive. Can we bump sidecar pool and move model registry through internal egress proxy that multiplexes connections? @nina can you schedule a tiny rollout?

nina: I can flip a feature flag to route model pulls through egress-proxy in us-west-2 only. 2-phase rollout over 30 mins. will also reduce per-pod concurrency to 8.

ops-oncall: noted. i'll put a temporary alert on natgw_port_utilization and tcp_timewait_count. also doing an emergency NATGW scale request with infra.

maria: adding small note: observed socket linger in sidecar logs -> `setsockopt SO_LINGER` being ignored, lots of sockets stuck in TIME_WAIT for 1-2 min.

alex: could help to enable tcp_tw_reuse/tcp_tw_recycle at host-level? (aware recycling has issues with NAT)

jon: tcp_tw_recycle is bad with NAT; will break clients behind different NATs. not recommended. tcp_tw_reuse might be okay but test carefully. better: enable keepalive with longer keepalive_time but fewer new connections.

kevin: alternative: implement source port rotation in egress-proxy so multiple source IPs/ports shared more efficiently. also add short-lived port pooling on ENIs. AWS limits are painful.

maria: putting a quick playbook in case it happens again: 1) flip egress-proxy for model registry -> route through 1-2 multiplexed proxies  2) reduce per-pod concurrency to 8 3) scale NATGW or add secondary NATGW with new allocation pools 4) monitor timewait and conntrack 5) rollback to cached model snapshot if pulls keep failing.

nina: rolling egress-proxy now in canary (us-west-2a). will keep concurrency change in the same rollout so we can correlate.

sre-bot: ALERT muted: natgw_port_utilization_us-west-2 > 80% for 12m -> triggering autoscale request ticket #INC-2026-122

ops-oncall: autoscale request accepted for +2 NATGWs; ETA 8m. keep eye on packet drops.

maria: after canary flip, initial telemetry looks better: NATGW connections down ~40% and failure rate on workers reduced from 7% -> 0.4%.

alex: nice. follow-up: let's schedule a config change to sidecars to reuse http keepalive pools by default and add exponential backoff to parallel model pulls.

kevin: long term: explore VPC egress multiplexing service or moving model registry into same VPC to avoid NAT entirely for these pulls.

maria: will capture action items in the incident doc and tag platform/networking for long-term design. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
